items.label: 1A
items.claim: The UIUC Carver Biotechnology Center, a large public core, runs the NovaSeq 6000 alongside its NovaSeq X Plus and keeps the 6000 for a use case the X cannot serve.
items.detail: The Carver DNA Services instrument page (search-result text, Oct 2026) lists both the NovaSeq X Plus, labelled new, and the NovaSeq 6000. It notes the 6000 runs 2x250nt reads, which the X Plus does not offer. Carver bought the X Plus in Mar 2023 for $1,078,438, and the May 2024 trustee item says it owns six Illumina sequencers, so the 6000 has been kept for 3+ years after the X purchase. Read length is a reason for some 6000 volume to stay beyond a price-driven conversion. I did not verify the number of 6000s.
items.source_name: Carver Biotechnology Center, DNA Services (search-result text)
items.why_new: Gives a technical, read-length reason for 6000 persistence at a research core, which is not among the known tail cohorts.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: A public university core has had a sole-source reagent contract with Illumina since at least 2009, and its annual ceiling stayed flat in nominal terms from 2018 to 2024.
items.detail: Trustee filings show about $3.0M/yr (2012–13, renewed 2015 and 2017), then $5.0M/yr from Jul 2018 with renewal options to Jul 2024. The May 2024 item sets $25.0M over Jul 2024–Jun 2029 with one five-year renewal option, i.e. $25M ÷ 5 = $5.0M/yr. The ceiling rose 67% ($3M→$5M) in 2018, then 0% from 2018 to 2029, even though Gb per dollar has risen sharply. A ceiling is an authorization, not spend, so it signals a budget cap rather than a price. The contract uses Illumina sole-source language with no competitive rebid.
items.source_name: Univ. of Illinois Board of Trustees purchase recommendations (2012–2024; search-result summaries)
items.why_new: The known list has only the 2024 ceiling and the 2018 discounts; the full $3M→$5M→$5M/yr series is new, though it is a ceiling and not spend.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: The Carver reagent ceiling of $5M/yr set for 2024–29 is unchanged from the 2018–24 ceiling, which does not point to a large step-up in budgeted consumables volume at this core.
items.detail: The 2024 renewal was set at $25M for 5 years, the same $5M/yr as in 2018. Carver took an X Plus in Mar 2023 after that. A flat dollar authorization over 11 years at a core that added X capacity suggests spend is capped by budget (research funding) rather than by sequencing cost. That fits thesis 1C and 2A, but a ceiling can also simply be padded. Treat it as an indicator and not a measurement.
items.source_name: Univ. of Illinois Board of Trustees (2019 renewal item, search-result summary)
items.why_new: This adds the 2019 first-renewal data point to the known 2024 ceiling and shows the ceiling did not rise.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: The Carver instrument list shows no Element AVITI or Ultima, and I found no trustee item for a non-Illumina sequencer at Illinois.
items.detail: Carver's DNA Services page lists Illumina X Plus, 6000, MiSeq i100 and MiSeq, plus PacBio Revio and an ONT GridION, but no AVITI or Ultima as of the search results. The search found no 2025–26 trustee purchase item for a competitor. This is a watch-out: in this large Big Ten core, price competition from new short-read rivals has not yet reached the instrument list.
items.why_new: This is a negative check on a Big Ten flagship core, which is not covered by the known core cards.

notes: Only the University of Illinois trustee agendas indexed. The binary .docx and PDF files (May 2024, Mar 2023, Mar 2018/2019, May 2017) could not be parsed with the tools available (no Bash or Python), so dollar figures are from search summaries and are unverified. Searches for UT System, UC Regents, SUNY, Purdue, Michigan, Wisconsin, Minnesota and Ohio State sole-source Illumina board items returned only federal notices. A later agent with Python can open the saved files and run `python -I` on word/document.xml in the Mar 2023 and May 2024 docx files. Check whether the May 2024 item gives per-year amounts, discount tiers or a competitive-bid note, and look for fall 2025 or spring 2026 amendments. A search of the UT System Regents 'contract report' PDFs and the UC Regents 'Illumina' items is worth one more try with different wording.
